summary: The Siamese fighting fish is an air-breathing labyrinth fish kept in many selectively bred colours and fin shapes. Males defend territories and should be housed separately; the species naturally occupies shallow, vegetated waters in Southeast Asia.
nativeRange: Southeast Asia; captive ornamental strains are widely bred.

features: Upturned mouth, suited to taking food at the surface.
Ornamental males often have bright colours and extended fins; wild fish are less showy.
An extended anal fin runs along the underside of the body.

habitat.description: Shallow rice paddies, ponds and slow streams with dense vegetation.
habitat.diet: Small insects and larvae, supplemented in captivity with suitable prepared and frozen foods.
